_README: Copy this to %USERPROFILE%\.horizun\live-fixtures.json and fill it in with REAL
values for this machine. scripts/verify-live.ps1 reads it; an explicit -Parameter
WHY IT LIVES OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY. Every value here names something real - a
model title, a shared-parameter file, a project folder. Committing them, or
putting them in CI variables, republishes exactly the client and project names
that this policy exists to keep out. The file the release gate reads
must not be the file that leaks what it is checking.
A value left blank makes its probes NOT COVERED - named in the output, and under
-ReleaseGate a non-zero exit. That is the intended behaviour: a guarantee missing
from the output reads exactly like one that passed.
_Document: Title of a model open in the Revit under test. Without it, links, quantities and the whole confirmation flow are NOT COVERED.
_InactiveDocument: Title of a SECOND model open in the SAME Revit but NOT active. It must really be open and really not active: the probe that used to pass a title matching nothing exercised the no-match path and proved nothing.
_SpfPath: Full path to a real shared-parameter .txt file. Needed for the bind_shared_param rehearsal probe - a rehearsal that refuses because the file is missing proves nothing about whether it stops before the transaction.
_SpfParam: The name of a definition inside that SPF.
_QuantityCategory: A category that EXISTS in the model under test. quantities correctly refuses to report zero for an empty category, so a category from a different model leaves the probe unverified.
_OldFile: Full path to a real .rvt or .rfa saved by a DIFFERENT Revit version, for the upgrade guard.
_WriteDocument: Title of a DISPOSABLE model open in the Revit under test, for the -WriteProbes tier.
Every other probe in this harness is non-destructive: the write commands are exercised
through their refusals and dry runs. That is safe, and it is also why place_sprinklers,
connect_mep and terminate_riser reached review with their apply paths never once executed.
Refusals prove the guards. Only a commit proves the command.
So this tier COMMITS. It needs a model nobody minds it writing into, and it never saves:
make a copy, mark the copy read-only on disk, open it, and name it here. A workshared
central should be opened DETACHED so nothing can reach the central.
The probes find their own targets by querying the model (pipe types, system types, a level,
a sprinkler symbol, a vertical pipe), so this is one title rather than a dozen element ids
that would go stale on the next save.
_WriteDocumentDisposable: Must be exactly 'yes-this-model-is-disposable'. Anything else, including blank, makes every
write probe NOT COVERED and nothing is written.
A second, deliberate opt-in on top of -WriteProbes: the switch says what kind of run this is,
this says the named model is really expendable. One flag is easy to pass by habit; the point
of two is that the model is named in the same breath as the permission to write into it.
_VoidFamilyDocument: Title of a FAMILY document, open in the Revit under test, containing at least one VOID form
that cuts a solid. For the family_mirror_void write probe.
A void earns its keep by cutting. The four properties that command verifies - present, still
a void, cuts the same number of solids as its source, landed where the reflection puts it -
cannot be checked against a family that has no void, and a family with only solids exercises
just the refusal. Four families on this machine were checked and none had one.
It takes two minutes to make: new family from any template, one extrusion, a second extrusion
set to Void that overlaps it, Cut Geometry, save as its own .rfa, open it, name it here.
_ClosedWorksetDocument: Title of a local WORKSHARED fixture model. It may already be open: the harness copies its saved file
to a disposable temporary path and opens that copy with ClosedWorksetName kept closed.
This is the one condition in the product that cannot be detected from inside the answer it
corrupts. A closed workset's elements are not in the document, so a scan does not skip them -
it never sees them - and every count comes back smaller with nothing anywhere reporting a gap.
'0 imported CAD instances' over a half-loaded model is a true statement about what was loaded,
presented as a statement about the building.
It cannot be simulated either: whether a workset is open is a property of how the model was
opened. Any local workshared fixture will do; it does not have to be the same one as Document.
A COPY OF A CENTRAL IS STILL A CENTRAL. Measured 2026-09-03 on Revit 2026: a file copied from a
central and named ..._L is refused by the typed open as a central, and opening it with
detach=true renames the document to '<title>_detached' - so the title a scan must be given is
NOT the one in ClosedWorksetDocument. Declare that title in ClosedWorksetDetachedTitle when the
fixture is a detached copy; leave it empty when the fixture is a real local.
_ClosedWorksetName: Exact user-workset name the typed open must keep closed.
_ClosedWorksetDetachedTitle: The title the document ends up with when the fixture is opened detached, when that differs
from ClosedWorksetDocument. Empty for a real local. This exists because the difference is
invisible until a scan is refused for naming the wrong active document.
